title: Universal Skipped-Release Update and Automatic Safe Schema Migration
summary: Allows every exact supported public release to update directly through declared automatic-safe schema transitions, with durable migration attempts, writer quiescence, strict target readiness and schema-independent recovery truth.
changelog: Supports direct updates from each exact supported public tag through the real declared historical schema transitions.
Runs preparation, recovery, migration and readiness checks in one ordered schema-update one-shot before product writers start.
Keeps database control and attempt records as operation decision state, with signed stage receipts as bound derived evidence.
Allows proven exact-target startup when no update is active even if one regular stale derived receipt remains after interruption.
Preserves the v0.7.24 request, status and admission handoff used by supported direct updates.
Keeps public update status read-only while authenticated controller and retry paths retain mutation authority.
Preserves users, roles, cameras, settings, recording metadata, archive roots and generated multi-root mounts.
Combines update-check and active execution truth, with restart and temporary 502 tolerant polling.
Uses the application confirmation modal and prevents raw proxy or backend response text from reaching users.
Keeps strict validation at external and released-format boundaries without claiming synthetic internal parser hardening.
Restricts permission checks and repair to the explicit privileged execution chain instead of recursively normalizing the product tree.
Always checks owner, symlink and mode evidence, and inspects ACLs when supported getfacl evidence is available.
Rejects unsafe special mode bits and supported writable ACL evidence, clearing special bits only on the privileged chain.
Keeps permission gates integrated with install, update, release preparation, helper images and API bootstrap dependencies.
Requires the resolved GitHub repository to match the descriptor and verifies matching local and remote annotated tag evidence.
